title: Letters and Tide
premise: Astrid Winterbourne has built her career on erasing herself, ghostwriting the memoirs of celebrity chef Margaux Delacroix—her former mentor turned rival. When her sister's wedding forces Astrid home to the coastal town she fled a decade ago, she hires local boatbuilder Elias Thorne to pose as her boyfriend, never expecting him to be the man whose wrongful conviction her testimony helped secure years ago. As their fake romance deepens into something real, Astrid uncovers evidence that could clear Elias's name but destroy Margaux's memoir and Astrid's career with it. In the end, Astrid chooses justice over invisibility: she testifies at the reopened hearing, loses her contract but gains her own byline, and stays in the tide-worn town where Elias finally asks her for a real first date.
about_author: Rosalind Nakamura spent seven years as a ghostwriter before publishing under her own name, an experience that taught her how much of a life can live between someone else's lines. She writes from a converted fishing cottage on the Oregon coast, where the tide charts on her kitchen wall are more decorative than practical.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She finishes a chapter of Margaux's memoir in a New York apartment she can barely afford, then receives her sister's wedding invitation demanding a plus-one. The beat is quiet desperation—the moment she realizes her invisible life has no one in it.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Back in Port Merrow for the reunion weekend, she impulsively hires Elias Thorne, a boatbuilder she meets at the harbor, to pose as her boyfriend for two weeks. Their contract is signed over chowder. The beat is nervous comedy masking old wounds about homecoming.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner, Real Stakes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The fake couple performs flawlessly at the rehearsal dinner until Astrid's mother mentions the trial from ten years ago. Elias goes rigid; Astrid notices but doesn't understand. The beat is dread seeded beneath charm.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought Back
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Alone sanding a hull, he reveals to the reader that Astrid was the prosecution's star witness who identified him near the marina fire that killed his business partner. He took the plea deal to protect someone. The beat is bitter irony—he's falling for her again anyway.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. At the family brunch, the performance stops being performance: they finish each other's jokes, and her grandmother blesses them. Walking out, Elias almost tells her the truth and doesn't. The beat is warmth curdling into guilt.

chapters.title: Margaux's Version of Events
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. On a video call, Margaux reveals the memoir includes a chapter about 'the Port Merrow tragedy'—and demands Astrid's firsthand account as the witness. Astrid realizes her ghostwritten words could reopen wounds. The beat is the past arriving as a deadline.

chapters.title: The Boathouse Confession
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Rain traps them in his boathouse; he finally tells Astrid who he is. She is shattered—her identification sent an innocent man to prison while she built a career on reinvention. The beat is devastation and the strange relief of truth.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Wrong
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. She digs through her old notes and finds gaps: her memory of that night was coached by the prosecutor, who was dating Margaux's sister. The beat is righteous fury turning toward purpose.

chapters.title: Contract Renewal
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They agree to stay 'together' through the wedding—for real this time—as allies investigating the case. The fake-dating trope inverts: now the pretense hides partnership, not romance. The beat is wary trust.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Knew
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Her sister Priya admits she saw the real arsonist the night of the fire but was paid off by the Delacroix family to stay silent. The beat is betrayal inside the found-family theme—blood loyalty tested against justice.

chapters.title: Margaux's Draft
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Reading Margaux's memoir draft, Astrid finds a buried paragraph admitting the fire was insurance fraud orchestrated by the family. Proof exists—in Margaux's own files. The beat is the trap closing: expose it and breach her NDA, ending her career.

chapters.title: Low Tide
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias tells Astrid to walk away; he survived prison once and won't let her burn for him. She refuses. First real kiss, angry and certain. The beat is love declared as defiance.

chapters.title: The Wedding
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Priya's wedding is beautiful and tense; Astrid gives a toast about second chances that doubles as a promise to Elias. The prosecutor attends as a family friend. The beat is bittersweet joy with the antagonist in the room.

chapters.title: Files and Firewalls
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. With Priya's help, they copy the Delacroix financial records linking the fire to an insurance payout. The prosecutor's investigator notices them. The beat is thriller-quick escalation.

chapters.title: Blacklisted
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Margaux discovers the copies, terminates Astrid, and threatens legal ruin. Astrid's agent drops her. Standing in her empty rental, she has nothing left to lose. The beat is rock bottom reframed as freedom.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Astrid recants her coached testimony before the conviction integrity unit, presenting the records and Priya's statement. The prosecutor implodes on cross-examination. The beat is cathartic climax—justice spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Exoneration
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The court vacates the conviction. Elias walks out into sunlight and sea air, ten years late. His mother embraces him; Astrid waits at the edge of the crowd, unsure of her place. The beat is grief and grace entwined.

chapters.title: What Remains of Me
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. Careerless, she drafts her own story—not a ghost's, hers—and sends it to a small independent press. Elias, overwhelmed, pulls away to figure out who he is without the conviction defining him. The beat is necessary solitude.

chapters.title: The Byline
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV. The press accepts her essay; a literary agent calls about a full memoir. For the first time, success arrives with her name on it. The beat is earned triumph, quiet rather than loud.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Elias finishes restoring his father's derelict sloop and names it after the day he was freed. He realizes Astrid never saw him as a case or a cause—only as himself. The beat is readiness.

chapters.title: Letters and Tide
chapters.summary: Both POVs converge. Elias finds Astrid at the harbor at dawn and hands her a letter she once ghosted for him years ago, returned unopened—proof she always mattered. He asks her on a real first date. The beat is the title made flesh: everything unsaid, finally delivered.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Astrid's POV, epilogue-style. One year later: her memoir is published, Priya's family has reckoned with its secrets, and Astrid signs her book in the boathouse where it began. Elias sails them out past the breakwater. The beat is belonging—not found, but chosen, daily.
